definition: Deep Linguistic Processing with HPSG - INitiative (DELPH-IN) is a collaboration where computational linguists worldwide develop natural language processing tools for deep linguistic processing of human language.
details: The goal of DELPH-IN is to combine linguistic and statistical processing methods in order to computationally understand the meaning of texts and utterances. The tools developed by DELPH-IN adopt two linguistic formalisms for deep linguistic analysis, viz. head-driven phrase structure grammar (HPSG) and minimal recursion semantics (MRS). All tools under the DELPH-IN collaboration are developed for general use of open-source licensing. Since 2005, DELPH-IN has held an annual summit. This is a loosely structured unconference where people update each other about the work they are doing, seek feedback on current work, and occasionally hammer out agreement on standards and best practice.

explainer.lead: DELPH-IN is a worldwide collaboration building open-source tools that analyse both the grammar and meaning of human language. It matters because understanding a sentence takes more than spotting words: computers also need structured information about how those words fit together and what they express.

tiers.eli5: Imagine trying to understand a sentence by using both a grammar puzzle and a meaning map. DELPH-IN is a group of language researchers sharing computer tools for doing both jobs, rather than everyone building their own from scratch. Their tools are open for others to use, and the group meets each year to compare work and agree on useful shared practices.
tiers.practitioner: DELPH-IN is not a single software package but a collaboration around open-source tools for deep linguistic processing. Applications combine linguistic and statistical methods, using HPSG for grammatical analysis and MRS for semantic representation. A common pitfall is treating it as a purely statistical NLP framework or expecting one unified tool instead of interoperable work developed across the collaboration.
tiers.paperLevel: DELPH-IN can be summarized as: linguistic processing + statistical processing -> computational analysis of meaning in texts and utterances. Its deep-analysis formalisms are head-driven phrase structure grammar (HPSG) and minimal recursion semantics (MRS), with tools developed for general use under open-source licensing. Since 2005, its annual summit has also provided a setting for feedback and occasional agreement on standards and best practice.

explainer.example: A researcher could process the sentence "The cat sleeps" with DELPH-IN tools: HPSG-based analysis describes its grammatical structure, while MRS provides a representation of its meaning. Statistical methods can complement this linguistic analysis within the broader goal of computationally understanding language.

explainer.intuition: A sentence can be analysed on two connected levels: how its words are grammatically arranged and what meaning that arrangement conveys. DELPH-IN provides a shared setting for building tools that work at both levels and combine them with statistical processing.
howItWorks: Start with human language in the form of a text or utterance.
Apply linguistic and statistical processing methods rather than relying on either approach alone.
Use HPSG to support deep analysis of grammatical structure.
Use MRS to represent semantic information.
Share the resulting open-source tools and, through the annual summit, exchange feedback and develop common practices.
explainer.whyItMatters: DELPH-IN lets researchers build on shared formalisms and open-source tools instead of developing every component independently. Its annual unconference also helps participants exchange feedback and occasionally agree on standards and best practice.
misconceptions: DELPH-IN is a collaboration and collection of tools, not one single NLP program.
Its approach is not purely statistical; it explicitly combines linguistic and statistical processing.
HPSG and MRS serve different roles: HPSG supports grammatical analysis, while MRS represents semantics.
